questions.q: What does including `hashFiles('package-lock.json')` in a cache key accomplish?
options: The cache automatically becomes invalid — and gets rebuilt — whenever dependencies change
It deletes the cache after every run
It makes the cache available to every repository on GitHub
It encrypts the cache contents
questions.explain: Hashing the lockfile ties the cache key to the exact dependency versions, so a changed lockfile produces a new key and a fresh cache instead of a stale one.

questions.q: What does `restore-keys` do when no exact cache key match is found?
options: Deletes all caches for the repository
Forces the workflow to skip caching entirely
Fails the job immediately
Restores the most recent cache whose key starts with the given prefix
questions.explain: restore-keys is a fallback — GitHub searches for the most recent cache matching that prefix rather than starting completely from scratch.

questions.q: What is the core difference between a cache and an artifact?
options: A cache is downloadable from the run summary; an artifact is not
A cache speeds up a future run; an artifact preserves what the current run actually produced
An artifact can only store dependencies, never test reports
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: Caching is about reuse between runs (dependencies, toolchains); artifacts are about keeping a specific run's output (reports, builds) for download or hand-off.

options: How long the job itself is allowed to run
How often the cache key is recalculated
How many times the artifact can be downloaded
How many days GitHub keeps the artifact before automatically deleting it
questions.explain: retention-days sets the artifact's lifespan on GitHub's storage before it's automatically removed.

questions.q: How can a later job in the same workflow run use a file uploaded earlier with upload-artifact?
options: It cannot be accessed again once uploaded
Only by manually downloading it from a browser first
By pulling it back down with actions/download-artifact
It automatically appears on every subsequent runner without any action
questions.explain: actions/download-artifact retrieves a previously uploaded artifact inside the workflow, which is how storefront passes a build output from one job to the next.
